en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape and its history of frequent, explosive eruptions.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for seeing in the dark.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake on the island and the second-largest in the country, supplying water to hydroelectric plants.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level and hosting rare wildlife.
The Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found in Mount Kitanglad, produces the largest individual flower in the Philippines and smells like rotting meat to attract pollinators.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over six hundred species of marine life.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool and dry weather to the Philippines between November and February, ideal for harvesting crops like rice.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, with the laterite nickel mines of Surigao del Norte supplying international manufacturing markets.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over two thousand years ago for irrigating rice paddies.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, inhabits the rainforests of Mindanao and hunts monkeys and colugos from the high forest canopy.
